en: Dependent on a state that is not an outflow (anāsava), a state that is not an outflow arises by way of the root condition (hetupaccaya).

Dependent on a state that is not an outflow, a state that is not a non-outflow (nanoāsava) arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is not an outflow, states that are both not an outflow and not a non-outflow arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not an *āsava*, a state that is an *āsava* arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is both not an *āsava* and an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both not an *āsava* and an *āsava*, a state that is an *āsava* arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is both not an *āsava* and an *āsava* … [and so forth].
Dependent on a state that is neither an outflow nor a non-outflow, states that are neither an outflow nor a non-outflow arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of root; nine in the case of object … pe … one in the case of result … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Full detail for all.)
